\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{قسط} (qisṭ)}{قسط (qisṭ)}]{\ar{قسط} (qisṭ) — an instalment; a share}

\label{lesson:AR-C453-qist}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to change money, then the Arabic for to deposit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{قسط}}
\textbf{\ar{قسط}} — \emph{qisṭ} — \textquotedblleft{}an instalment; a share\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{دفع} \ar{أبي} \ar{قسط} \ar{السيارة} \ar{هذا} \ar{الشهر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dafaʿa abī qisṭ as-sayyāra hādhā ash-shahr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father paid the car instalment this month.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{أقساط}, \emph{aqsāṭ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{قسط}} (\emph{qisṭ}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-s-ṭ}, \textquotedblleft{}a fair share, a portion\textquotedblright{} (Lane).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qisṭ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qisṭ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dafaʿa abī qisṭ as-sayyāra hādhā ash-shahr.} — My father paid the car instalment this month.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to change money, then the Arabic for to deposit, then say \emph{qisṭ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{قسط} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An instalment; a share\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{نقدا} (naqdan)}{نقدا (naqdan)}]{\ar{نقدا} (naqdan) — in cash}

\label{lesson:AR-C453-naqdan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to deposit, then the Arabic for an instalment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{نقدا}}
\textbf{\ar{نقدا}} — \emph{naqdan} — \textquotedblleft{}in cash\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{دفعت} \ar{ثمن} \ar{التذكرة} \ar{نقدا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dafaʿtu thaman at-tadhkira naqdan.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I paid for the ticket in cash.
\end{quote}

The noun \emph{naqd} is cash; the ending \emph{-an} makes the adverb.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{نقدا}} (\emph{naqdan}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-q-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to pick out good coins\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Naqd} is ready money.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{naqdan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{naqdan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dafaʿtu thaman at-tadhkira naqdan.} — I paid for the ticket in cash.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to deposit, then the Arabic for an instalment, then say \emph{naqdan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{نقدا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}In cash\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{صراف} \ar{آلي} (ṣarrāf ālī)}{صراف آلي (ṣarrāf ālī)}]{\ar{صراف} \ar{آلي} (ṣarrāf ālī) — a cash machine}

\label{lesson:AR-C453-sarraf-ali}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for an instalment, then the Arabic for in cash.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{صراف} \ar{آلي}}
\textbf{\ar{صراف} \ar{آلي}} — \emph{ṣarrāf ālī} — \textquotedblleft{}a cash machine\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{سحبت} \ar{مالا} \ar{من} \ar{الصراف} \ar{الآلي}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{saḥabtu mālan min aṣ-ṣarrāf al-ālī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I took money out of the cash machine.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{صراف} \ar{آلي}} (\emph{ṣarrāf ālī}) is a modern coinage built from two native Arabic words (Lane gives both roots): \emph{ṣarrāf}, \textquotedblleft{}a money changer\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{ṣ-r-f}, and \emph{ālī}, \textquotedblleft{}mechanical\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{āla}, \textquotedblleft{}a machine\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{ʾ-w-l}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣarrāf ālī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saḥabtu mālan min aṣ-ṣarrāf al-ālī.} — I took money out of the cash machine.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for an instalment, then the Arabic for in cash, then say \emph{ṣarrāf ālī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{استرد} (istaradda)}{استرد (istaradda)}]{\ar{استرد} (istaradda) — to get back (money); to recover}

\label{lesson:AR-C453-istaradda}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for in cash, then the Arabic for a cash machine.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{استرد}}
\textbf{\ar{استرد}} — \emph{istaradda} — \textquotedblleft{}to get back (money); to recover\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{استرددت} \ar{ثمن} \ar{التذكرة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{istaradadtu thaman at-tadhkira.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I got the price of the ticket back.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يسترد}, \emph{yastaridd}.

A doubled verb: \emph{istaradda}, \textquotedblleft{}he got back\textquotedblright{}, but \emph{istaradadtu}, \textquotedblleft{}I got back\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{استرد}} (\emph{istaradda}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-d-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to send back, to return\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form X, \textquotedblleft{}to ask for back\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istaradda}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istaradadtu thaman at-tadhkira.} — I got the price of the ticket back.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for in cash, then the Arabic for a cash machine, then say \emph{istaradda} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{عداد} (ʿaddād)}{عداد (ʿaddād)}]{\ar{عداد} (ʿaddād) — a meter (that counts)}

\label{lesson:AR-C453-addad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a cash machine, then the Arabic for to get back.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{عداد}}
\textbf{\ar{عداد}} — \emph{ʿaddād} — \textquotedblleft{}a meter (that counts)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كان} \ar{العداد} \ar{في} \ar{التاكسي} \ar{معطلا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāna al-ʿaddād fī at-tāksī muʿaṭṭalan.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The meter in the taxi was out of order.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{عداد}} (\emph{ʿaddād}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-d-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to count\textquotedblright{} (Lane). The pattern \emph{faʿʿāl} names a thing that does a job: the counter.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿaddād}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāna al-ʿaddād fī at-tāksī muʿaṭṭalan.} — The meter in the taxi was out of order.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a cash machine, then the Arabic for to get back, then say \emph{ʿaddād} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
